title: Hosted API: Tenant Residence Selector and Auto-Evidence Scheduler
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Provide a tenant-level UI and API primitive that lets customers pick a residency preference for Hosted API endpoints and attach a scheduled evidence export job. The feature exposes: 1) a Residence Selector (GUI + API) that supports 'Soft Pin' (preferred region ordering), 'Hard Pin' (strict residency enforcement), and 'Opt-Out' options; 2) a Retention/TTL config for stored payloads and audit logs; 3) an Auto-Evidence Scheduler that bundles periodic attestable export packages (manifest + sampling proof + routing trace) and ships them to a configurable storage destination.

Background / problem:
Compliance teams require an easy way to declare where their Hosted API data is processed and to obtain repeatable, machine-verifiable evidence proving residency and retention behavior. Existing controls are fragmented (routing knobs, region preference fields, manual ad-hoc exports) and lack a single tenant-scoped experience that ties intention to verifiable exports. This causes lengthy manual audits and slows enterprise procurement.

Goals:
- Give customers a clear, discoverable control to declare residency intent per tenant and endpoint.
- Surface the expected enforcement semantics (soft vs hard) and the consequences (request rejection vs routing fallback).
- Provide scheduled automated evidence exports (bundle + checksum + provenance) on a cadence customers can rely on for audits.
- Instrument routing decisions and retention actions for later replay in evidence bundles.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement on-prem private datapaths or cross-cloud encrypted proving. Those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant UI exposes a Residence Selector with three options (Soft Pin, Hard Pin, Opt-Out) and a per-tenant description of enforcement semantics
Tenant API (PATCH /v1/tenants/:id/residency) allows programmatic setting of residency mode and preferred region list
Routing layer accepts per-tenant residency metadata and honors Hard Pin by rejecting requests that cannot be satisfied in the pinned region (returning 409 with residency_reason)
Soft Pin routes preferentially but will fallback to a secondary region if SLOs would otherwise be missed
Retention settings UI and API allow configuring TTL for request payload cache and audit logs; retention actions are recorded in audit log

Auto-Evidence Scheduler can be configured (daily/weekly/monthly), generate a deterministic bundle (manifest.json, routing-trace.ndjson, sample-requests.json, signature.sig) and deliver to a tenant-provided S3/GCS location
Evidence bundles include KMS-backed signature metadata and a checksum; UI shows last successful export and link to the destination
E2E tests and a canary run with 5 opt-in tenants complete without regression to API latency >5% at p95
Documentation (Console walkthrough + API spec + compliance guide) is published to the docs site and linked in the UI
tasks: Design: final console mocks for Residency Selector and Evidence Scheduler (DES handoff)
API: add residency resource and PATCH endpoint; update tenant schema and validation rules
Routing: plumb per-request tenant-residency header through smart-router and implement hard-pin reject path
Scheduler: implement evidence export orchestration worker with chunked upload and retry semantics
Storage: add signed manifest generation and KMS envelope metadata to evidence bundles
Observability: add telemetry events (residency.decision, evidence.export.started/completed/failed) and dashboard panels
E2E: create integration test harness that simulates region failure and verifies hard-pin rejects and soft-pin fallbacks
Docs & Compliance: draft compliance-ready report template and add export verification steps
notes: Design trade-off: prefer explicit tenant-level opt-in for Hard Pin because accidental hard pinning can cause user-facing rejections. Default to Soft Pin for new tenants.
We will surface enforcement consequences inline (e.g., 'Hard Pin may return 409 if capacity unavailable in pinned region').
Evidence bundles are intentionally 'sampling-first' — full request dumps require opt-in and will have separate data-retention controls.
Signed manifest uses existing KMS integration; if customer supplies their own key URI we include a key identifier but not the key material.
This feature will be behind a feature flag and gated for tenants on enterprise plans during initial rollout.
